### The EFF short word list 2.0 (`packages/core/src/own-address/words.ts`)

(<https://www.eff.org/files/2016/09/08/eff_short_wordlist_2_0.txt>), which EFF publishes under the Creative Commons
Attribution 4.0 International licence (<https://www.eff.org/copyright>). Changed: 300 words removed. The conformance

## Not open source

These are fetched under their own terms. They are not part of this repository, not covered by its licence, and
nothing in it grants rights in them.

### Claude Code (Anthropic)

Claude Code is proprietary software: “© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to the Legal Agreements
outlined here: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance>.” It is not open source, Whombat’s licence does not
cover it and grants nothing in it, and it is used under Anthropic’s own terms.

- **This repository** pins it as optional dependencies of `packages/agent-runtime` (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-arm64@2.1.302`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.302`) and contains none of it:
  `pnpm install` downloads the binary for the machine’s architecture from the npm registry.
- **Whombat’s builds** leave it out: the runtime bundle (`pnpm bundle:runtime`) keeps it external and its manifest says
  `claude.bundled: false`; the web, widget and admin pages and the Android and iPhone apps don’t contain it.
- **On an appliance** it is not in the image. On an owner’s request the manager downloads it from Anthropic’s own
  download site (`downloads.claude.ai`), at the version Whombat tested: Whombat’s signed client channel
  (`appliance/release-tools/clientchannel`) names its address, size and SHA-256, and the box installs Anthropic’s
  file, unmodified, only when it matches. Until every Whombat runs a manager that does this, Whombat’s update host also
  keeps that unmodified binary for older ones.

### Hermes Agent and agent-browser

`pnpm hermes:install` installs, for development, Hermes Agent 0.23.3 (Nous Research,
<https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent>, MIT, below) from its git tag with the Python packages its `uv.lock`
pins, each under its own licence, and agent-browser 0.26.0 (Vercel, <https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser>,
Apache-2.0) from the npm registry (`packages/hermes-whombat/agent-browser.json`). The appliance image builds both in
(`appliance/nix/packages/hermes`), and its notices list them too. The agent’s skills are Hermes’s own: its
built-in and optional skills come with Hermes under its MIT licence, and each skill an owner installs from Hermes’s
hub keeps its own licence.

```text
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2025 Nous Research

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
```

## Dependencies

Installed by the package manager from `pnpm-lock.yaml` (production dependencies of every workspace
package); they are not part of this repository. Each package's own licence file applies. The runtime bundle
(`pnpm bundle:runtime`) lists every package it contains, with its licence text, in its `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`.

Every licence below allows distributing Whombat under AGPL-3.0-only (`pnpm notices` fails on any other):

| Licence | Packages | Next to the AGPL |
|---|---|---|
| MIT | 752 | permissive |
| ISC | 64 | permissive |
| BSD-3-Clause | 25 | permissive |
| Apache-2.0 | 23 | compatible with GPL-3.0 and the AGPL; attribution and NOTICE files required |
| BSD-2-Clause | 11 | permissive |
| BlueOak-1.0.0 | 6 | permissive |
| Unlicense | 6 | permissive |
| MPL-2.0 | 3 | file-level copyleft: changes to those files stay MPL-2.0; combining them with the AGPL is allowed (MPL-2.0 section 3.3; none is marked “Incompatible With Secondary Licenses”) |
| 0BSD | 2 | permissive |
| OFL-1.1 | 2 | fonts, used as fonts and never relicensed |
| CC-BY-4.0 | 1 | attribution required (browser data) |
| CC0-1.0 | 1 | permissive |
| MIT-0 | 1 | permissive |
| Python-2.0 | 1 | the PSF licence, GPL-compatible |

Where a package offers a choice, Whombat uses it under the most permissive licence it offers; these also offer one that couldn't be combined with the AGPL: @zone-eu/mailsplit (MIT OR EUPL-1.1+: MIT), node-forge (BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0: BSD-3-Clause).
